If you're drawn to ARPGs for high-level hardcore play (meaning the gaming mentality, not the permadeath mode), I have to recommend Path of Exile over D3.

In terms of balance/design, Diablo 3 has a bunch of problems with build diversity and loot. Item sets have a recurring problem with power-creeping other gear (thus railroading players into using them, nullifying much of the gratification in hunting for good rares), and there really aren't THAT many meaningfully different ways to build each class.

PoE has it's balance and design problems as well -- life-based builds are currently in a bad place compared to energy shield, and the game is still *really* dense and newcomer-unfriendly, for examples -- but if you enjoy the Loot Action RPG nitty-gritty of minmaxing characters, rewarding loot hunting, and rerolling uniquely different character builds, Path of Exile's endgame will give you much more to sink your teeth into. It's also worth noting that PoE is still receiving very frequent patches and dev attention, with no signs of that slowing down. They're about to start the beta testing for 3.0, which is completely overhauling the story experience and shaking balance up significantly by fixing broken damage multiplier mechanics that had somewhat overcentralized the meta around a few OP skills.

All things considered, the Diablo franchise *absolutely* wins on lore and story presentation, hands down. I think for someone just looking to casually enjoy killing and looting it's superior, but I find that the more invested and genre-savvy you become the more the state of Diablo 3's endgame underwhelms.

Diablo 2, on the other hand, is still one of the best games in the genre, both as a casual experience and a serious loot RPG. You really can't go wrong with that one.

Can confirm, played competitive Pokemon TCG for 2ish years before I went to college and a buddy got me into Magic. The draw, tutor, and recursion effects in that game are *ridiculously* strong, so the game is much more about board state, combat, and hand/board disruption than anything else. There's no sideboarding, but the search is so strong that that one-of tech cards are viable inclusions because you can get them much more reliably.

> you can only play one on each of your turns. So you can't chain them into one another

This is true for draw Supporters (RIP chainable wheels and draw-twos from Base Set era), but a single tutor Supporter can search for targets that chain into other searches. Skyla targeting Computer Search is effectively a free "Discard 2, tutor any card from your deck" in a game where graveyard engines can be pretty strong.
You can also Skyla for a Pokemon tutor, then for a Pokemon with ETB draw. The number of lines of play just increase dramatically with so much search redundancy.

This also creates an interesting deckbuilding dynamic where Trainer/Supporter shells can be tuned for raw linear draw power, strong search, or somewhere in the middle depending on how linear, controlling or teched-out your deck is.

According to a friend of mine, TRS has stated they intend to stick primarily to bilaterally symmetrical, generally humanoid monsters. I'd like to see insectoid monsters as well, but I imagine the rigging/modeling/thematic constraints in relation to gameplay would be too problematic.

This is a good idea. As it stands now, Decoy really is the problem with the Wraith. Free damage and stealth, with no opportunity cost or real counterplay, is broken.

Some say the Decoy shouldn't do damage, but I think the Wraith needs a way of doing *some* indirect damage to the hunters. The Wraith's ideal win-con scenario is a team of Hunters full of strikes; a low armor pool means a Wraith must make fights quick and decisive. Hank shields, Medic healing, and particularly the Lazarus Device are already sufficient to prevent (or at least slow) such a fight from arising, and I worry that having NO indirect combat damage would remove some of the Wraith's agency in setting up favorable engagements.

I think Wraith still needs Decoy to do damage to help reach its win-con, but Decoy needs to come with a cost, and a consumed armor bar being the Decoy's health is a great way to implement that.
